subtitle: Eight chapters, forty-five experiments: step by step on paper, live on your phone.
back_lead: Can a machine think? The question is very old. What is new is that the machines that can try to answer it are now sitting on the table.
back_text: A two-century story, from the first calculating gears to today’s chatbots: rules, search, probability, learning, neurons, attention. Each idea was born where the one before it hit a wall, and the chapters follow that order.

Forty-five experiments are worked out on paper with real numbers: you make a Turing machine add 1, fire a neuron, pull a picture out of noise. The QR code under each figure opens the live version of the same experiment on your phone; no sign-in needed.

The book is written at two depths. The main text is for readers with no background at all; the “Technical depth” boxes are for anyone who wants the formula and the math. Skip the boxes and nothing is missing.
author_bio: Onur Önder is an engineer working in data, artificial intelligence and software, and a co-founder of Fittechs.
The real problem is that we cannot tell when we need to learn what. This book sets out to solve that very problem.
I am glad to share a source you need to read closely in order to understand and digest one of the most radical transformations and revolutions in the history of humanity and technology.
Get ready to learn, from the ground up, the real source of the developments we may face in the years ahead.
You can find the interactive digital edition of this book at book.onuronder.com. Scan the QR codes to see the live version of the figures inside the book.
